# <em>EDA in R</em> {#sec-eda-basic}

[Modeling in Python](model-basic-py.qmd) fit a linear model to the `penguins` data. The `eda-basic.qmd` file runs an exploratory data analysis (EDA) of the same data in R. It groups the penguins by species and sex, summarizes the means of the numeric columns, and plots body mass against bill length.

Expand the section below to view the source file: 

<details>
  <summary><strong>View eda-basic.qmd</strong></summary>
  
<br>

```{r}
#| label: print-eda-basic-qmd
#| echo: false
library(readr)
readr::read_lines("_labs/lab01/eda-basic.qmd") |> 
  base::noquote() |> 
  writeLines()
```

</details>

I've also included the code from the `eda-basic.qmd` file in the sections below. 

## Load data

The code below loads `palmerpenguins`, `dplyr`, and `ggplot2` and stores the `penguins` data as `df`:

```{r}
#| label: eda-basic-qmd-pkgs
#| message: false
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

df <- palmerpenguins::penguins
```

## Manipulate and summarize

The pipeline below returns a table with the mean of every numeric column by species and sex:

```{r}
#| label: eda-basic-qmd-wrangle
#| warning: false 
#| message: false
df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(species, sex) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::where(is.numeric), 
      \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    ) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

The table should have eight rows: female and male for each species, plus a row for the Adelie and Gentoo penguins with a missing (`NA`) `sex`.

## Visualize

The scatter plot below shows body mass against bill length, with a linear fit line for each species:

```{r}
#| label: eda-basic-qmd-viz
#| warning: false 
#| message: false
df %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = bill_length_mm, 
      y = body_mass_g, 
      color = species)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() + 
  ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

Each species should get its own colored line, and the Gentoo points should sit above the Adelie and Chinstrap points.

## Recap

1. The `eda-basic.qmd` file loads `palmerpenguins::penguins`, groups the data by `species` and `sex`, and uses `dplyr::across()` with `where(is.numeric)` to compute the mean of every numeric column.

2. The scatter plot of `body_mass_g` against `bill_length_mm` adds a `geom_smooth(method = "lm")` line for each species. The model in [Modeling in Python](model-basic-py.qmd) estimates this relationship with one shared slope: body mass increases with bill length, and species and sex shift the baseline.

Next, [Lab 2: Project Architecture](lab02.qmd) loads the penguins data into `duckdb` and turns the model into a `vetiver` API.
